data.name: Ahram
data.gender_notes: Ahram is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'ahram', meaning 'great' or 'mighty'. In Islamic tradition, this name is associated with the Prophet Ibrahim, who was known for his great faith and obedience to Allah. The name Ahram carries the meaning “Fame, Greatness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ahram usually hope their child will grow to embody fame, greatness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of spiritual enlightenment and inner peace.
data.etymology: Ahram belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fame, Greatness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ahram total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ahram' holds significant cultural importance in Islamic tradition, as it is connected to the ancient Islamic pilgrimage to Makkah, known as the Hajj. The first few days of this pilgrimage are called 'Ahram Days', during which pilgrims wear special clothing called 'Ihram', indicating their intention to perform the Hajj.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Ahram' serves as a powerful reminder of the greatness and might of Allah. The Prophet Ibrahim, who is associated with this name, demonstrated unwavering faith and obedience to Allah, inspiring countless generations to follow his example. The 'Ahram Days' of the Hajj pilgrimage also serve as a time for believers to reflect on their faith, pray, and seek forgiveness, deepening their spiritual connection with Allah.
